title: Build Android, Windows and Linux from one PowerShell command
changes: The existing Docker PowerShell launcher accepts android and all alongside windows and linux. A single platform exports to its selected directory. A combined build puts each platform in its own directory and stops at the first failure.

Android delegates to the maintained port launcher with its working-tree filter, Docker toolchains, caches, signing and checksum validation. The script checks for host Python 3.9+ before starting an Android or combined build. An interactive failure waits for Enter.
validation: PowerShell 7.4.6 on Linux exercised default and explicit platform selection, paths with spaces, combined output layout, failure propagation and early exit. All 12 launcher and Android adapter checks passed. A pseudo-terminal acknowledged the failure with Enter and a missing-Python check stopped before the combined build (bng6em3q).
The real Android path exported the maintained APK into dist/docker-android with a matching SHA-256 and reports for 29 passing Kotlin tests from the Docker cache (sop1z5h8).
limitations: Desktop routing used a simulated Docker CLI in this validation. Native Windows PowerShell 5.1 and Docker Desktop were not exercised.

The initial scratch export succeeded but validation retained its diagnostics after encountering a symlink in the extracted test shell (a09tlc7u). A subsequent terminal probe timed out with Read-Host (176_qtfg). The final check passed with console input.
